analysis.title: The Home Improvement Mosaic - Read-Throughs to 3Q26
key_insights: GS sales-weighted vendor index rose +1% y/y in 3Q26, flat vs 2Q's +1%. Two-year stacked was +1% y/y (-2% in 2Q) and three-year stacked was -1% y/y (-3% in 2Q).

Vendor and retailer read-throughs were mixed, leaning slightly negative. Select vendors cite continued macro uncertainty and muted 2026 outlooks, higher costs going into 4Q, and pro/commercial outpacing residential and DIY.
HundredX data show LOW ahead of HD among overall and DIY consumers on NPS and NPI in Sep'26. HD remains ahead among Pro customers.
HD and LOW report 3Q26 on November 17th and 18th. Consensus (FactSet) expects HD same-store sales of +1.7% (GS +2.2%) and LOW +0.1% (GS +0.0%).
For EPS, consensus expects HD $3.83 (GS $3.88) and LOW $2.87 (GS $2.86).
The 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 6.9% in September, up from 6.7% in Aug'26. NAHB remodeling index slowed to +3.3% in 3Q from +3.4% in 2Q.

Census building materials and garden dealer sales rose +4.6% y/y in September after +5.5% in August (NSA). 3Q through September was +5.1% y/y vs 2Q's +4.9%, but two-year stacked slowed to +2.3% from +3.6% and three-year to +1.4% from +1.8%.
Average visits per venue were negative y/y in Oct'26 for both HD (-1%) and LOW (-2%) per Placer.ai.
HD led LOW on price favorability (29.0%) and value favorability (35.6%) as of Sept'26. Over the last year LOW's value favorability rose +0.6pp to 35.2% while HD's fell -0.3pp.
GS Lumber Composite Index was 140.1 for the week ending 10/30 vs a 3Q average of 146.7, flat q/q and +22.3% y/y. It is down 69% from the May 2021 peak of 454.7 and up 17.8% y/y as of 10/30.
Copper averaged 41.8% above the March 2022 peak in October. 3Q26 (Aug-Oct) copper averaged +42.5% y/y and +6.6% q/q.
Houzz construction sector: expected business activity 74.0 in 4Q26 (61.0 in 3Q26, 66.0 in 4Q25), backlog 5.5 weeks (6.1 in 3Q26), recent activity 55.0 in 3Q26 (47.0 in 2Q26).
Houzz architecture sector: expected activity 62 in 4Q26 (68 in 3Q26), backlog 4.9 weeks (4.7 in 3Q26), recent activity 53 in 3Q26 (62 in 2Q26).

September housing data: single-family permits -4.0% m/m to 0.85mn, starts -4.6% to 0.86mn, existing-home sales +1.5% m/m to 3.99mn with supply at 4.8 months. NAHB Housing Market Index fell to 32 from 35.
HD trades at 21.3x NTM P/E (117 relative to the S&P 500) vs a 1-year average of 22.1x. LOW trades at 16.7x (91 relative) vs a 1-year average of 17.7x.
Appliance exposure is 9% of HD sales and 14% of LOW sales. Paint is 7% of HD sales and 5% of LOW sales.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy ahead of 3Q26 results on Nov 17. The target is based on relative P/E multiples of 90%/100%/105% (downside/base/upside).
GS reiterates Buy ahead of 3Q26 results on Nov 18. The target is based on relative P/E multiples of 80%/90%/95% (downside/base/upside).
3Q26 North America sales rose +5% in local currency and FY26 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $4.65-$4.75 from $4.40-$4.60. GS calls it a positive read-through for HD and LOW.
3Q26 organic sales rose +4% and FY26 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $5.95-$6.25 from $5.20-$5.80. GS calls it a positive read-through for HD and LOW.
North America sales (ex-FX) fell 8.2% y/y and full-year net sales guidance was lowered to about $14.5bn. GS calls it a negative read-through for HD and LOW.
3Q26 volumes fell -4% and management expects flooring conditions to soften in 4Q26 and market volumes to decline in 2027. GS calls it a mixed read-through.
Paint Stores Group sales rose 4.7%, but DIY demand stayed muted and management expects muted demand into 2027. GS calls it a mixed read-through.
3Q26 net sales rose +4% y/y, but gross margin fell 60bps on freight and customer mix. GS calls it a mixed read-through.

sector_views.rationale: Vendor sales are soft (+1% y/y) and read-throughs lean slightly negative. Pro demand outpaces DIY, and housing turnover remains weak with mortgage rates at 6.9%.

earnings_insights: HD 3Q26 preview, reports Nov 17: consensus (FactSet) same-store sales est +1.7% vs GS est +2.2%. EPS consensus est $3.83 vs GS est $3.88. Not yet reported.
LOW 3Q26 preview, reports Nov 18: consensus (FactSet) same-store sales est +0.1% vs GS est +0.0%. EPS consensus est $2.87 vs GS est $2.86. Not yet reported.
MAS reported 3Q26 on Oct 28: North America sales +5% in local currency, Plumbing +8%. FY26 adjusted EPS guidance raised to $4.65-$4.75 from $4.40-$4.60.
MHK reported 3Q26 on Oct 29: net sales +1% y/y to $2.8bn (flat adjusted). 4Q26 adjusted EPS guidance is $1.35-$1.45 with +LSD adjusted sales growth.
POOL reported 3Q26 on Oct 22: net sales +4% y/y, gross margin down 60bps y/y, equipment sales +5%, chemicals +4%.
ELUX reported 3Q26 on Oct 23: US market demand fell about 5%, and the FY26 volume/price/mix outlook was cut to a neutral operating income contribution.
SWK reported 3Q26 on Nov 4: net sales $3.7bn (-1% y/y), organic +4%. FY26 adjusted EPS guidance raised to $5.95-$6.25 from $5.20-$5.80, helped by a $0.17/$0.67 net tariff benefit in 2Q/3Q.
SHW reported 3Q26 on Oct 27: Paint Stores Group sales +4.7%, Consumer Brands Group +21.7% (Suvinil acquisition, mix, FX). Full-year sales guidance maintained at up MSD to HSD.
SMG reported 4Q26 on Nov 4: U.S. Consumer segment sales -10% for the quarter and +1% for the full year. FY27 net sales growth guided to +2% to +4%.
WHR reported 3Q26 on Oct 26: North America sales (ex-FX) -8.2% y/y with industry demand -3.3%. A further 7% price increase takes effect December 3 in the U.S.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 6.7% in August, which raises the cost of home purchases and weighs on housing turnover.

macro_indicators.indicator: Building Material and Garden Equipment retail sales y/y
macro_indicators.interpretation: Down from +5.5% in August. Two-year stacked growth improved to +4.8%.
Up 1.5% m/m, with supply unchanged at 4.8 months.
Down from 35 in August. Readings below 50 indicate an unfavorable outlook.
Flat vs the 3Q average of 146.7 and up 17.8% y/y.
Copper is above the March 2022 peak, which raises vendor input costs.

risk_factors: Comp sales could decelerate if housing turnover fails to recover or macro headwinds weigh on home improvement demand.
HD valuation could look high if the housing market enters a sustained slowdown.
Pricing could deteriorate from increased competition.
Margin pressure from lower demand and higher supply chain costs.
Tariffs and commodity costs, including copper up 42.5% y/y, are a headwind to vendor profitability.
Vendors expect mid-single-digit inflation to persist into early 2027.
